## Escalation notifications

Both settings are optional because the destination is undecided (`KU-14`).
Unset, the api starts normally, records escalations at
`no_destination_configured`, notifies nobody and logs one
`escalation.no_destination` warning at startup. In the chart,
`api.escalationWebhookSecretName` names a Secret with the keys `url` and,
optionally, `token`. The records live in the `escalations` collection, so a
record and its place in the retry schedule survive a restart. A record whose
process died mid-send is claimed again by the next process after 10 minutes, so
the destination may receive it twice.

# Support agent audit trail

## Problem Statement

`brief.md` § Constraints requires a vendor SLA that lets OLT meet its 24-hour, 72-hour and 1-month NIS-2 reporting windows, and those windows are filed against evidence. Nothing in the support agent records that a model was called. Today the only evidence a turn happened is a `console.log` line into whatever bucket Cloud Run happens to write to. There is no count of model calls, no record of which model answered, no record that a provider outage occurred, and no way to answer "how many customer questions did the agent handle in March" without reading logs that have already rotated.
